PROVIDENCE, R.I. [Brown University] — Most people know by now that artificial intelligence powers much of the online world, sifting social media posts, planning driving routes or helping to choose a movie to watch. But what goes largely unseen is the human labor — often people working for low wages in the Global South — that makes this careful algorithmic lifestyle curation possible.
